_notes: THE WEFT -- the magic system, and what the four humours MEAN.
data/energy_cards.json says what a humour COSTS. This says what it IS.
The split matters: a rules change should never need a writer, and a
rewrite of what Moonlight means to Ash should never need a programmer.
Humour ids MUST match Catalog.HUMOURS. The fourth humour's id is
`mysticism` for save-file stability and its name is Moonlight everywhere a
player can see it -- Catalog.validate() fails any content field that shows
the player the id, because the Parlor's hand-written rule card did exactly
that and shipped for a chapter.

weft.name: The Weft
weft.blurb: Threads of intention running through everything, visible to almost no one.
weft.truth: Magic is needlework. Witches stitch; cats read the stitching. You have watched a cat stare at an empty corner — that is what it was doing.

_notes: `nature` is the cat's own reading of it. `teaches` names the prologue
beat that introduces it, so a writer can find where a player first met
the idea before assuming they know it (the terms-before-explanation
defect, which every owner review has found at least once).

ferocity.name: Ferocity
ferocity.blurb: The red one. The oldest there is, and the only one a cat is born knowing.
ferocity.nature: Want, arriving faster than thought. It pays for the things you do before deciding to.
ferocity.teaches: prologue — the vole on the rooftop

guile.name: Guile
guile.blurb: The green one. Patience with a plan behind it.
guile.nature: Knowing which of the two doors is the one nobody watches.
guile.teaches: prologue — the wrong lamps, before the rag-wraith

shadow.name: Shadow
shadow.blurb: The black one. Being somewhere without having arrived.
shadow.nature: Not invisibility — unnoticeability, which is cheaper and lasts longer.
shadow.teaches: prologue — the gutter-wisp on Needle Lane

mysticism.name: Moonlight
mysticism.blurb: The blue one. Elspeth's unfinished magic, which Ash spends but cannot yet make.
mysticism.nature: The moon is the world's needle's-eye and moonlight is thread that has not been used yet. Thread that has not been used can still become any stitch — which is exactly why Moonlight can be spent in place of any other humour.
mysticism.it_does_not_refill: In the fiction this is HERS, put into Ash out of her own evenings, and it is finite. What a cat has of his own comes back with meat and sleep; the pale does not. He feels it go when he spends it and there is less of it every time. Narration describes it as a cold weight under the ribs that goes out of him and is not replaced — never as a resource he is managing.
mysticism.data_id_warning: The DATA id is `mysticism` and always will be (old saves name it). The player is only ever shown `Moonlight`. UI goes through Catalog.humour_name().

_notes: The rule that keeps the writing honest: thread pulled must come from
somewhere. Any working shown in-game states its price.
costs.rule: Thread pulled must come from somewhere: memory, warmth, years, luck.
costs.why: It keeps the fiction honest and makes mechanics-as-narrative easy — a cost the player pays in cards is the same cost the story is describing.

the_pockets.name: The Shadow-Stitched Pockets
the_pockets.blurb: Nine pockets sewn into Ash's shadow, one for each life — Elspeth's last finished working.
the_pockets.truth: Anything Ash can carry in his mouth slides into a pocket and travels weightless wherever his shadow goes. Losing a life tears a pocket, which is where the Hollow Court's Toll comes FROM rather than merely what it costs.
the_pockets.open_thread: What happens when all nine have been torn and re-sewn — and whose stitching repairs them, if the Needle is dead.
